record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and other figure/table material have extraction artifacts, but the scaling section is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in image diffusion models, an application beyond text language-model pretraining, and reports FID and validation NLL across model sizes and training compute.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results only for image diffusion models. Results cited from other work and unrelated experiments are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 6 trains four ImageNet 64×64 diffusion UNets (30M–270M params) over about 1e17–1e20 FLOPs and fits power-law trend lines to FID and validation NLL against compute. That is a direct result on V5's claim that the power-law form holds beyond text pretraining.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors call the scaling results preliminary and say DDPMs 'improve in a predictable way' with training compute. FID looks power-law-like; NLL fits less cleanly, possibly from high irreducible loss or overfitting. The conclusion states more compute 'trivially leads to better sample quality and log-likelihood'.
record.recipe_differences: This is an image diffusion-model scaling study, not a language-model pretraining scaling study; it measures FID and image validation NLL.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling behavior differs by metric: FID appears more cleanly power-law-like than validation NLL.
record.problems: The scaling results are reported in Figure 10 without tabulated numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The authors describe the scaling results as preliminary and say validation NLL does not fit a power law as cleanly as FID.

untested.parts: Only image diffusion on unconditional ImageNet 64×64 is tested, over about 3 orders of compute and 30M–270M params. Video, other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. Parameter or data scaling laws are not separately fitted.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
Width is scaled by a channel multiplier, but shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.
No comparison of fitting choices or published laws.

missing.what: The fitted exponents (FID -0.22, NLL -0.17) and how the irreducible constants were set. The FID constant came from the FID of in-distribution data and the NLL constant from rounding down the Routing Transformer SOTA. The constants were hand-chosen, not fitted, and the compute axis assumes full hardware utilization.

Overfitting on class-conditional ImageNet 64×64, where FID worsens late in training. The authors conclude it is better to early stop and grow model size than to spend more compute on training time. This is a qualitative remark on how to spend extra compute.

record.verdict_notes: This is mainly a diffusion-methods paper; scaling is a small preliminary section with one figure. No tabulated values or uncertainties are given. The power-law fits use hand-set irreducible constants, so how well the power law fits depends on that choice. The eight per-model rows overstate granularity: the evidence is two joint trend lines, one for FID and one for NLL.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test held-out pretraining loss in language models.
The paper does not test whether fits from small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
The paper does not find or test a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
The paper does not test architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Tests image diffusion models on ImageNet 64 × 64, scaling model capacity and training compute. It does not test video, other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
FID and validation NLL are reported, but the paper does not test downstream-task performance.
The paper notes that the NLL curve fits a power law less cleanly, but does not test whether fitted laws or compute-optimal allocations depend on setup or fitting choices.
